mainTopic: מכשירי מצוה on שבת for the פסח: רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא, the הזאה dispute, and the rule that preparations override שבת only for someone already fit
overview: This amud continues the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא about whether preparations for the קרבן פסח (מכשירי מצוה) override שבת. רבי אליעזר argues that if preparations after the שחיטה override שבת, preparations before it should too. רבי עקיבא answers that after the שחיטה, שבת has already been set aside, while before it, it has not. Next comes a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא uses הזאה as proof, a rule he says he learned from רבי אליעזר himself. עולא's attempt to explain the contradiction (תרומה versus פסח) is rejected. The גמרא concludes that רבי אליעזר forgot his own teaching and רבי עקיבא respectfully tried to remind him. רבה explains that הזאה is forbidden as a safeguard against carrying in רשות הרבים. The answer to why רבי אליעזר does not permit it anyway is that מכשירי מצוה override שבת only for someone already fit for the מצוה. רבה and רבא apply this to heating water for מילה, and אביי challenges it from the ערל who gets כרת. רבה begins his answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר holds a מצוה-related rabbinic prohibition can be set aside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רבי אליעזר does not accept the earlier קל וחומר: in his view, a שבות done for a מצוה is more important.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר? He holds that a שבות for the sake of a מצוה is preferable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is defending רבי אליעזר from the argument made on the previous amud. It says he would answer that a rabbinic prohibition can give way when a מצוה is at stake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier argument said: if a שבות is not permitted for ordinary יום טוב needs, surely it is not permitted on שבת. רבי אליעזר answers that the comparison fails, because a מצוה has extra importance that ordinary needs do not have. So the קל וחומר does not work against him.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic prohibition on שבת or יום טוב (not a Torah-level מלאכה)
For the sake of a מצוה
In his view it is preferable or stronger

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer (how does he answer this?)
phrases.notes: This points back to the קל וחומר from the previous amud.

phrases.english: A rabbinic prohibition for a מצוה is preferable to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי אליעזר against the קל וחומר from יום טוב raised on the previous amud
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a מצוה-related שבות differs from an optional one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a שבות is forbidden for ordinary יום טוב joy, it must be forbidden for a מצוה on שבת
steps.terutzMaskana: A שבות for a מצוה is weightier, so it may be permitted even when an optional שבות is not

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's argument from preparations after the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר: if preparations done after the שחיטה override שבת, then preparations done before it should override שבת too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר said, 'Consider this. If preparations for the מצוה done after the שחיטה override שבת, even though the מצוה has already been done, shouldn't preparations done before the שחיטה override שבת?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר argues his position directly using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the שחיטה, the main מצוה is already finished, yet its follow-up preparations still override שבת. Before the שחיטה, the מצוה has not happened yet and still depends on these preparations. So רבי אליעזר argues they should be even more permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Preparations that enable a מצוה (not the מצוה act itself)
When the מצוה has already been done

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר's wording 'וּמָה לִי' here means 'Consider this, if...' and introduces a קל וחומר. Do not read it as a dismissal.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer said:
Consider: if they override

phrases.aramaic: מַכְשִׁירֵי מִצְוָה שֶׁלְּאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: the מצוה preparations after the slaughter override Shabbat,
phrases.notes: For example, rinsing the innards, which everyone permits

phrases.english: even though the מצוה has already been done,
should the מצוה preparations not override
that come before the slaughter, Shabbat?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא showing רבי אליעזר's own reasoning for permitting preparations before the שחיטה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Preparations before the שחיטה should override שבת, a fortiori from preparations after the שחיטה

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: after the slaughter, Shabbat is already overridden
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects the קל וחומר. After the שחיטה, שבת has already been set aside; before the שחיטה, it has not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: 'How can you compare them? Preparations after the שחיטה override שבת because the שחיטה has already overridden שבת. Can you say preparations before the שחיטה should override שבת, when the שחיטה has not yet overridden it?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא breaks רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר by pointing to a key difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the שחיטה has happened, שבת has already been pushed aside for this קרבן, so a further rabbinic act is not a fresh break. Before the שחיטה, no override has happened yet, so allowing preparations would start a new break of שבת. The point is that the 'after' case is actually easier to permit, not harder.

keyTerms.meaning: How is this comparable? (here it rejects the comparison)
Since the slaughter has already overridden

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
How is this comparable? If they override
phrases.notes: Here the phrase rejects the comparison

phrases.aramaic: מַכְשִׁירֵי מִצְוָה שֶׁלְּאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: the מצוה preparations after the slaughter override Shabbat,
that is because the slaughter already overrode Shabbat;
would you say that the מצוה preparations override
that come before the slaughter, Shabbat,
when the slaughter has not yet overridden Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: דְּמָה לִי אִם דָּחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר of רבי אליעזר
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the קל וחומר only; it does not reject the general importance of מצוה preparations
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'after' case has a leniency the 'before' case lacks: שבת has already been overridden

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's second reason: the offering might turn out invalid
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא adds another reason. The animal might be found פסול, and then the person would turn out to have broken שבת for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another reason: perhaps the offering will be found invalid, and it will turn out, looking back, that he desecrated שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a second, separate reason not to allow preparations before the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you do preparations before the שחיטה and the animal then turns out to have a blemish, no מצוה was done at all. The שבת violation would then have had no מצוה to justify it. This reason has nothing to do with the קל וחומר; it is a practical risk.

phrases.english: Another reason:
perhaps the offering will be found invalid,
and he will turn out to have desecrated Shabbat retroactively.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: שֶׁמָּא יִמָּצֵא זֶבַח פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an independent second reason against רבי אליעזר
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects permitting any pre-slaughter preparations on שבת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Permitting them risks a שבת violation that turns out to serve no מצוה

steps.title: If so, the slaughter itself should be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's second reason: the same worry would forbid the שחיטה on שבת too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, we should not slaughter either, since perhaps the offering will be found invalid, and he will turn out to have desecrated שבת retroactively!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי עקיבא's second reason by showing that it proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שחיטה itself is a Torah-level מלאכה, and everyone agrees the פסח is slaughtered on שבת. Yet the same risk exists there: the animal could turn out פסול after the שחיטה. If that risk does not stop the שחיטה, it should not stop the preparations either.

phrases.english: If so,
we should not slaughter either,
since perhaps the offering will be found invalid,
and he will turn out to have desecrated Shabbat retroactively.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי — מִשְׁחָט נָמֵי לָא נִשְׁחֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second reason given in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reason that the offering might be found invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: the same worry would forbid the שחיטה, which is clearly permitted on שבת

steps.title: The order was reversed: the second reason was said first and refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי עקיבא first gave the 'invalid offering' reason, רבי אליעזר refuted it, and then רבי עקיבא gave the 'after the slaughter' reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי עקיבא said that reason to him first, and רבי אליעזר refuted it. Then he said to him this other reason: 'How is this comparable? If they override...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the problem by reordering the conversation. The weak reason was raised first and dropped, and the final, standing reason is the 'after the slaughter' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא accepts that the 'invalid offering' reason does not hold up, for exactly the reason given in step 5. It says רבי אליעזר made that objection himself, so רבי עקיבא abandoned the reason. רבי עקיבא's real, surviving argument is that preparations after the שחיטה come once שבת has already been overridden.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר permits preparations before the שחיטה on שבת, reasoning from the preparations after it. רבי עקיבא forbids them. His standing reason is that after the שחיטה, שבת has already been overridden, while before it, it has not. The 'invalid offering' reason was refuted and dropped.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא lists the 'invalid offering' reason second, but the גמרא says it was actually said first and rejected. Do not treat it as רבי עקיבא's final position.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: הָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ בְּרֵישָׁא וּפַרְכֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rather: he said this to him first, and he refuted it,
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר refuted the 'invalid offering' reason

phrases.english: and then he said to him that other reason:
'How is this comparable? If they override...'
phrases.notes: Quotes the opening words of רבי עקיבא's reason from step 3

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ בְּרֵישָׁא וּפַרְכֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by reordering the dialogue in the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reordering the sequence of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא held both reasons at the end, so the 'invalid offering' reason is open to attack
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'invalid offering' reason was said first and refuted by רבי אליעזר. רבי עקיבא's final argument is the 'after the slaughter' distinction.

steps.title: The משנה's line: רבי עקיבא brings proof from sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line where רבי עקיבא uses הזאה as proof against רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: רבי עקיבא answered and said, 'הזאה proves it,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא it is about to bring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא argues that הזאה is done for a מצוה and is only forbidden מדרבנן, yet it still does not override שבת. So the preparations for the פסח should not override שבת either. The גמרא now looks at what happened between the two of them after this argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the purifying water of the פרה אדומה on someone who is טמא
Will prove it, as in a proof case

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva responded and said:
Sprinkling will prove it, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה. 'Etc.' points to the rest of רבי עקיבא's argument there.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְאָמַר: הַזָּאָה תּוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier ברייתא about the order of the arguments back to the משנה's line about הזאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הזאה, which is a מצוה and only a שבות, does not override שבת, and רבי עקיבא uses this as proof.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's sharp reply to רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי אליעזר rebuked רבי עקיבא and said his death would be by slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר said to him, 'עקיבא, you answered me with an argument about שחיטה. Your death will come through slaughter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows how strongly רבי אליעזר reacted to רבי עקיבא's argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא had flipped the קל וחומר to argue that even שחיטה should not override שבת. רבי אליעזר saw this as disrespectful, since it went against a clear tradition. So he answered harshly, matching the punishment to the topic.
steps.confusionAlert: 'His death' means רבי עקיבא's death. רבי אליעזר speaks about him in the third person. The words are a sharp rebuke, not a new halachic argument.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
Akiva, with slaughter you answered me,
by slaughter will his death be.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא describing רבי אליעזר's reaction to the משנה's argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר harshly rejects רבי עקיבא's reversed argument about שחיטה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: I learned this rule from you
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that he received from רבי אליעזר himself that הזאה is a שבות and does not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'My teacher, do not reject what I say now that we are arguing. This is what I received from you: הזאה is a שבות, and it does not override שבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא defends himself. He points out that his proof case comes from רבי אליעזר's own teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basis of רבי עקיבא's argument, that הזאה does not override שבת, is not his own idea. It is a tradition he learned from רבי אליעזר himself. So רבי אליעזר should not reject it now.

keyTerms.meaning: I have received as a tradition
An act forbidden on שבת only מדרבנן

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's next question. If רבי אליעזר taught this rule himself, why did he argue against it?

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher,
do not reject me at the time of the argument,
this is what I received from you:
sprinkling is a rabbinic prohibition,
and it does not override Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי, אַל תַּכְפִּירֵנִי בִּשְׁעַת הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא answers רבי אליעזר's rebuke by citing רבי אליעזר's own teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That his proof from הזאה is valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: A tradition רבי עקיבא received from רבי אליעזר himself: הזאה is a שבות and does not override שבת

steps.title: Why did רבי אליעזר go back on his own teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר disagreed about הזאה if he himself taught that it does not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since רבי אליעזר himself taught him this, why did he go back on it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction in רבי אליעזר's view and asks how to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר argued that even הזאה should override שבת. But רבי עקיבא says רבי אליעזר taught him the opposite. The גמרא wants to know how one person could hold both views.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back on it, retracted

phrases.english: But since he himself taught him,
what is the reason he went back on it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּהוּא אַגְמְרֵיהּ, מַאי טַעְמָא קָא הָדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי עקיבא's claim from the ברייתא to point out a contradiction in רבי אליעזר's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's position in the משנה that הזאה can override שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר himself taught that הזאה does not override שבת, so how could he argue the opposite?

steps.title: עולא: רבי אליעזר taught about sprinkling for תרומה
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that רבי אליעזר's teaching was about הזאה for תרומה, which does not override שבת because תרומה itself does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: When רבי אליעזר taught him, he taught him about הזאה for eating תרומה. That kind does not override שבת, because תרומה itself does not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא solves the contradiction. He says there are two kinds of הזאה, and רבי אליעזר's teaching was only about one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sprinkling a כהן so he can eat תרומה cannot override שבת, because the matter of תרומה itself does not override שבת. But sprinkling someone so he can eat the קרבן פסח is different. רבי אליעזר may hold that this kind does override שבת, just as the פסח itself does.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether הזאה is a שבות. Both kinds are a שבות. The difference is what the sprinkling is for: תרומה or the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
When Rabbi Eliezer taught him,
he taught him about sprinkling for terumah,
for terumah itself does not override Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר כִּי אַגְמְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: the teaching was about a different kind of הזאה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר taught that all הזאה does not override שבת, so he contradicts himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: He taught this only about הזאה for תרומה. He can still hold that הזאה for the פסח overrides שבת.

steps.title: The misunderstanding: רבי עקיבא meant תרומה, רבי אליעזר heard פסח
steps.stepSummary: עולא continues: רבי עקיבא's challenge was also about הזאה for תרומה, but רבי אליעזר thought he meant הזאה for the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא also, when he challenged him, challenged him from הזאה for תרומה, which is a מצוה and is only forbidden as a שבות. But רבי אליעזר thought he was challenging him from הזאה for the פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא finishes his answer. He explains that the two rabbis misunderstood each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's proof was from הזאה for תרומה: it is a מצוה and only a שבות, yet it does not override שבת. רבי אליעזר thought the proof was from הזאה for the פסח. That is why he answered that he disagrees about that kind of הזאה too.
steps.whatToRemember: According to עולא, רבי אליעזר agrees that הזאה for תרומה does not override שבת. He argues only about הזאה for the פסח, and the two rabbis talked past each other.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva too, when he challenged him,
challenged him from sprinkling for terumah,
which is a מצוה, and is forbidden only as a rabbinic prohibition!
And he (Rabbi Eliezer) thought
that he was challenging him from sprinkling for the Pesach offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues עולא's answer by explaining רבי עקיבא's challenge and רבי אליעזר's misunderstanding.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's challenge was from הזאה for the פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא challenged from הזאה for תרומה, and רבי אליעזר wrongly took it as הזאה for the פסח.

steps.title: רבה: רבי עקיבא explicitly spoke about sprinkling on ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבה challenges עולא from a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא clearly brings proof from הזאה on ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה raised an objection: רבי עקיבא answered and said, 'Let the הזאה of a טמא מת prove it. His seventh day fell on שבת, and it was ערב פסח. The sprinkling is for a מצוה and is only a שבות, yet it does not override שבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks עולא's answer. He quotes a ברייתא showing that רבי עקיבא was talking about הזאה for the פסח, not for תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said רבי עקיבא's proof was from הזאה for תרומה. But this ברייתא says the case was a טמא מת whose seventh day fell on שבת that was also ערב פסח. That is clearly sprinkling so he can eat the פסח, which goes against עולא's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A person made טמא by contact with a dead body
The seventh day of his purification, when he is sprinkled
The day before פסח, when the קרבן פסח is brought

phrases.english: Rabba raised an objection:
Rabbi Akiva responded and said:
The sprinkling of one impure from a corpse will prove it,
whose seventh day happened to fall on Shabbat,
and on the eve of Pesach,
for it is a מצוה, and it is forbidden only as a rabbinic prohibition,
and yet it does not override Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's answer from steps 11 and 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that רבי עקיבא challenged from הזאה for תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows רבי עקיבא spoke about a טמא מת on ערב פסח that fell on שבת. That is clearly הזאה for the פסח, so the two did not misunderstand each other.

steps.title: עולא's answer is dropped: the teaching was about הזאה for the פסח
steps.stepSummary: After רבה's challenge, the גמרא rejects עולא's answer. It concludes that רבי אליעזר really did teach about הזאה for the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he certainly taught him about הזאה for the פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on עולא's answer. It says that רבי אליעזר's teaching to רבי עקיבא really was about הזאה for the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא had said the teaching was only about תרומה. רבה's ברייתא in step 13 showed that רבי עקיבא spoke about הזאה on ערב פסח. So the תרומה reading cannot stand, and the original problem from step 10 comes back.

phrases.english: Rather, certainly
he taught him about sprinkling for the Paschal lamb.
phrases.notes: This means רבי אליעזר taught רבי עקיבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רבה's challenge and rejects עולא's answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר's teaching to רבי עקיבא was about הזאה for the פסח, not for תרומה.

steps.title: The original problem returns: why did he argue with his own teaching?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אליעזר taught this himself, why did he object to it in the משנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And since he taught it to him, why does רבי אליעזר argue against it?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the teaching is about the פסח, the גמרא asks again its question from step 10. Why would רבי אליעזר argue against a rule he himself taught?
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's answer had removed this problem. With that answer gone, the contradiction inside רבי אליעזר's own views is back and needs a new solution.

phrases.english: And since he taught it to him,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא קָא פָּרֵיךְ לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר?
phrases.english: what is the reason Rabbi Eliezer argues against it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּאַגְמְרֵיהּ, מַאי טַעְמָא קָא פָּרֵיךְ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows directly from step 14's conclusion and brings back step 10's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's position in the משנה, where he argues about הזאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person would not argue against his own teaching, so how can רבי אליעזר object here?

steps.title: רבי אליעזר forgot his teaching, and רבי עקיבא reminded him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר forgot what he had taught. רבי עקיבא's argument was meant to remind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר's teaching was uprooted from him (he forgot it), and רבי עקיבא came to remind him of his teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר simply forgot his own teaching. רבי עקיבא's challenge was meant to jog his memory.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real contradiction in רבי אליעזר's views. He forgot the rule. רבי עקיבא's reasoning was designed to bring it back to his mind.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer forgot his teaching,
phrases.notes: Literally: his learning was uprooted from him.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Akiva came to remind him of his teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical explanation: the teacher forgot his own rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר seemed to hold two opposite views.
steps.terutzMaskana: He held one view but had forgotten it. רבי עקיבא was reminding him.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי עקיבא just say it plainly?
steps.stepSummary: If he wanted to remind him, רבי עקיבא should have said directly, 'You taught me this.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him say it to him openly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא used a roundabout argument. Why not just tell רבי אליעזר directly what he had taught?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying it directly would have been the clearest way to remind him. So the indirect method needs an explanation.

phrases.english: Then let him say it to him explicitly!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי עקיבא was trying to remind רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If reminding was the goal, a direct statement would have worked better.

steps.title: It would not have been respectful
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא felt it was not proper to tell his teacher openly that he had forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought: it is not proper conduct.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that telling a teacher 'you forgot' is disrespectful. So רבי עקיבא first tried to remind him gently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The indirect argument was a way of showing כבוד to his רבי. It let רבי אליעזר remember on his own instead of being corrected.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא's final picture: רבי אליעזר did teach that הזאה for the פסח does not override שבת. He forgot it, and רבי עקיבא respectfully tried to remind him through an argument.

phrases.english: He thought: it is not proper conduct.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explanation based on respect for a teacher.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The direct way should have been used.
steps.terutzMaskana: Respect for his teacher led רבי עקיבא to use the indirect way.

steps.title: Why should הזאה be forbidden on שבת at all?
steps.stepSummary: Sprinkling is just moving water. So why shouldn't it override שבת for the sake of the פסח?
steps.simpleTranslation: And הזאה, why does it not override שבת? After all, it is just moving something. Let it override שבת because of the פסח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question about the reason behind the rule. Sprinkling seems to be only moving water, so why not allow it for the פסח?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The act of sprinkling looks like simple handling, not a serious מלאכה. Something that minor should give way to the important מצוה of the פסח, so the ban needs a reason.

phrases.english: And sprinkling, what is the reason
that it does not override Shabbat?
After all, it is merely moving something,
let it override Shabbat for the sake of the Paschal lamb!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַזָּאָה מַאי טַעְמָא לָא דָּחֲיָא שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the story settled, the גמרא now questions the reason for the rule itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that הזאה does not override שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A minor act like moving water should give way to the important מצוה of the פסח.

steps.title: רבה: a safeguard against carrying in public
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis forbade הזאה so that people would not carry the water ארבע אמות ברשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is a גזירה, a safeguard, in case he picks it up and carries it ארבע אמות ברשות הרבים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains that the ban is a rabbinic safeguard. Someone might carry the water container four cubits in a public area, which is a real Torah prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sprinkling itself is not the main concern. The worry is what might happen along with it. The rabbis made a fence so that no one would come to break the Torah law of carrying.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבה uses this same kind of safeguard elsewhere, such as for שופר, לולב, and מגילה on שבת. It is a well-known pattern in his thinking.

phrases.english: Rabba said: It is a decree
lest he take it and carry it
four cubits in the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reason: a rabbinic safeguard.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sprinkling is minor, so it should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden as a fence against Torah-level carrying.

steps.title: But רבי אליעזר allows preparations for a מצוה on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that מכשירי מצוה override שבת. So he should even allow carrying the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי אליעזר, let us carry it! For רבי אליעזר said: preparations for a מצוה override שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's answer using רבי אליעזר's own rule. If preparations for a מצוה override שבת, carrying the water should be allowed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, even Torah-level carrying for a מצוה is allowed. So the fear of carrying should not matter to him, and he should not need the safeguard.

keyTerms.meaning: Actions that prepare or enable a מצוה

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Eliezer, let us carry it!
For Rabbi Eliezer said:
actions that enable a מצוה override Shabbat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer from the view of רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: Why רבי אליעזר agrees that הזאה does not override שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's rule would allow even real carrying for a מצוה, so the safeguard makes no sense for him.

steps.title: The rule only applies when the person is already fit for the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: מכשירי מצוה override שבת only when the person is fit and obligated. A טמא person is not yet fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: That rule applies when the man himself is fit and the obligation lies on him. But here, where the man himself is not fit, the obligation does not lie on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer limits רבי אליעזר's rule. It only works when the person is already able to do the מצוה. Someone who is טמא and still needs הזאה is not yet able.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Preparations may override שבת to carry out an obligation that already applies to the person. They may not be used to make a person fit in the first place. Since the טמא person is not obligated now, his הזאה does not override שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the מצוה is unimportant. The point is narrower: the person is not yet obligated, so preparations to make him fit do not override שבת.

phrases.english: They say: This applies
where the person himself is fit
and the obligation lies upon him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּגַבְרָא גּוּפֵיהּ לָא חֲזֵי —
phrases.english: But here, where the person himself is not fit,
phrases.notes: He is טמא, so he cannot eat the פסח yet.

phrases.english: the obligation does not lie upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּגַבְרָא גּוּפֵיהּ חֲזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by limiting רבי אליעזר's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of a general rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מכשירי מצוה always override שבת for רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: They override שבת only when the person is already fit and obligated.

steps.title: רבה applies the rule to heating water for a ברית מילה
steps.stepSummary: For a healthy baby, water may be heated on שבת for the מילה. For a sick baby, it may not, since he is not yet fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: According to רבי אליעזר, for a healthy baby we heat water to strengthen him and circumcise him on שבת, since he is fit. For a sick baby we do not heat water to strengthen him and circumcise him, since he is not fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה shows how the new limit works in practice with ברית מילה on שבת. He compares a healthy baby with a sick one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heating water is a preparation for the מצוה. For a healthy baby, who is already fit for מילה, רבי אליעזר allows it. For a sick baby, who is not yet fit, the same preparation does not override שבת, just like the טמא person needing הזאה.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר, מכשירי מצוה override שבת only to fulfill an obligation the person already has, not to make him fit for it. This is why הזאה for a טמא person, and heating water for a sick baby, do not override שבת.

phrases.english: Rabba said: According to Rabbi Eliezer,
for a healthy baby, we heat water for him
to strengthen him and circumcise him on Shabbat,
since he is fit for it.

phrases.aramaic: קָטָן חוֹלֶה — אֵין מְחַמִּין לוֹ חַמִּין
phrases.english: For a sick baby, we do not heat water for him
to strengthen him and circumcise him,
since he is not fit for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, קָטָן בָּרִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 22's limit to the case of מילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, water may be heated on שבת for the מילה of a healthy baby, but not for a sick baby who is not yet fit.

steps.title: Why would a healthy baby need hot water?
steps.stepSummary: רבא attacks the earlier distinction. If the baby is healthy, he does not need hot water to strengthen him in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And if the baby is healthy, why does he need hot water to strengthen him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the ruling from the previous step, which allowed heating water on שבת for a healthy baby's מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ruling assumed the hot water is needed for a healthy baby but not allowed for a sick one. רבא says this makes no sense. Hot water 'to strengthen him' only makes sense if the baby is in some way weak. So the case of a 'healthy baby who needs hot water' contradicts itself.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And if he is healthy,
why does he need hot water to strengthen him?
phrases.notes: He isn't really asking; he's challenging the idea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the internal logic of the healthy/sick distinction in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that water may be heated for a healthy baby's מילה on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A healthy baby needs no strengthening, so the case described cannot exist.

steps.title: All babies count as sick for circumcision
steps.stepSummary: רבא reformulates the rule. Every baby is considered 'sick' with respect to מילה, so for no baby may water be heated on שבת, since he is not yet fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Everyone is considered sick with regard to מילה. Whether the baby is healthy or sick, we do not heat water to strengthen him and circumcise him on שבת, because he is not yet fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces the old distinction with a new rule: all babies are treated the same, and none may have water heated for them on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every baby needs hot water around the מילה, so in that sense all babies are 'sick.' Because the baby is not yet fit for מילה until he has been strengthened, the principle from step 22 applies to every baby. מכשירי מצוה only override שבת when the person is already fit. The principle stays the same, but now it covers all babies.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying every baby is medically ill. He means that regarding מילה, every baby needs hot water, so all are in the 'not yet fit' category.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Everyone is considered sick regarding circumcision;

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד קָטָן בָּרִיא וְאֶחָד קָטָן חוֹלֶה
phrases.english: both a healthy baby and a sick baby,
we do not heat water for him
to strengthen him and circumcise him on Shabbat,
because he is not fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from step 24 by redefining the case so it covers all babies.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Healthy babies were thought to be fit, so water could be heated for them.
steps.terutzMaskana: All babies need hot water and so are not yet fit. No water may be heated for any baby on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: The 'not yet fit' principle now applies to every case of מילה, which sets up אביי's broader challenge to the principle itself.

steps.title: An uncircumcised man is still punished with כרת
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר holds that an ערל who did not circumcise himself gets כרת for missing the פסח. This shows that even someone currently unfit is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: An ערל who did not circumcise himself is punished with כרת; these are the words of רבי אליעזר. But here the man himself is not fit, and yet it teaches that he is punished with כרת. Apparently, the obligation rests on him!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the principle that a person who is not yet fit is not obligated. He uses a source from רבי אליעזר himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ערל cannot bring or eat the קרבן פסח, so right now he is 'not fit.' Even so, רבי אליעזר says he gets כרת for not bringing it. That means the obligation already rests on him while he is unfit. This contradicts the rule from step 22, which רבה applied in step 23 (and רבא extended in step 25).

keyTerms.meaning: the obligation is placed upon him

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
An uncircumcised man who did not circumcise is punished with karet;
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָכָא דְּגַבְרָא גּוּפֵיהּ לָא חֲזֵי,
phrases.english: But here, where the man himself is not fit,
and yet it teaches that he is punished with karet;
apparently, the obligation rests upon him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'not yet fit means not obligated' principle that steps 22 and 25 depend on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that according to רבי אליעזר, someone currently unfit is not yet obligated, so מכשירי מצוה do not override שבת for him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר gives כרת to an ערל, who is currently unfit. So for him, an unfit person still carries the obligation.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר does not slaughter for a טמא שרץ
steps.stepSummary: רבה responds that רבי אליעזר holds we do not slaughter the פסח or sprinkle its blood for someone who is טמא שרץ. Current unfitness does matter in his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: רבי אליעזר holds that we do not slaughter or sprinkle the blood for someone impure from a creeping creature.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends his principle by pointing to another view of רבי אליעזר. That view shows a person's present unfit state does count for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא שרץ can go to the מקוה and be pure by nighttime. Even so, רבי אליעזר says the קרבן is not slaughtered and its blood is not sprinkled for him while he is currently impure. So רבי אליעזר does treat 'not fit right now' as a real barrier when it comes to doing the קרבן. This is only the opening of רבה's answer. How it fits with the ערל being liable for כרת is worked out on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: slaughtering the קרבן and sprinkling its blood
one made impure by touching a dead creeping creature

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה (who answers here, as in steps 20 and 23) with רבא (who spoke in steps 24 and 25). The names look almost the same.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Rabbi Eliezer holds
that we do not slaughter or sprinkle the blood
on behalf of one impure from a creeping creature.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין וְזוֹרְקִין עַל טְמֵא שֶׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אביי's challenge by citing a parallel view of רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Supporting the principle from another ruling of the same תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ערל case proves רבי אליעזר ignores a person's current unfitness.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אליעזר, current unfitness does block the קרבן, as with a טמא שרץ. The full reconciliation with the ערל case continues on the next amud.
